observatories.name: Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array
observatories.place: Plains of San Agustin, near Socorro, New Mexico
observatories.description: A centimeter-wavelength radio observatory of 28 dishes, 25 m each (27 in use at a time), arranged in a Y shape and operated as one interferometer. It is run by the National Radio Astronomy Observatory.
observatories.highlights: Construction began in April 1973 and the array was formally inaugurated in 1980. Astronomers have used it for key observations of black holes and protoplanetary disks, and to find magnetic filaments at the Milky Way's centre. It appears in the 1997 film of Carl Sagan's Contact.
observatories.film: The VLA is a filming location of Contact (1997), the film of Carl Sagan's novel about a radio signal from another star.

observatories.name: Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA)
observatories.place: Chajnantor plateau, Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region
observatories.description: An interferometer of 66 radio antennas at about 5,000 m altitude that observes millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths. It is run by ESO, North American and East Asian partners together with Chile.
observatories.highlights: Its first images were released on 3 October 2011 and it reached full operational status in March 2013. It studies star and planet formation, dust and molecules in space, and early galaxies. Its wavelength range is 0.32 to 3.6 mm.

observatories.name: MeerKAT
observatories.place: Meerkat National Park, Karoo, Northern Cape
observatories.description: A radio telescope of 64 dishes, 13.5 m each, in South Africa's Karoo, run by the South African Radio Astronomy Observatory (SARAO). Originally the Karoo Array Telescope.
observatories.highlights: It was officially inaugurated on 13 July 2018 with an image of the region around the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way. In 2019 a team using it found balloon-like structures hundreds of light-years tall above and below the galactic centre. Its 64 dishes will be part of SKA-Mid.

observatories.name: Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT)
observatories.description: An array of thirty steerable 45 m dishes observing at metre wavelengths (50 to 1,500 MHz), run by the National Centre for Radio Astrophysics of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.
observatories.highlights: Built under Govind Swarup between 1984 and 1996, it is described as the largest and most sensitive radio telescope array at low frequencies. In August 2018 it detected TGSS J1530+1049, the most distant known radio galaxy at the time of that report. In February 2020 it contributed to observations of the Ophiuchus Supercluster explosion.

observatories.name: LOFAR (Low-Frequency Array), core at Exloo
observatories.description: A radio telescope of thousands of simple dipole antennas grouped in stations, with its core near Exloo and stations across Europe. It works at low frequencies (10 to 240 MHz) and is operated by ASTRON.
observatories.highlights: It was officially opened on 12 June 2010 by Queen Beatrix. As of 2019 it had 52 stations, 38 of them in the Netherlands. In February 2021 it released a high-resolution image of 25,000 active supermassive black holes covering four percent of the northern sky.

observatories.name: Large Millimeter Telescope Alfonso Serrano (LMT)
observatories.description: A 50 m single-dish millimeter-wave telescope at 4,850 m altitude on Sierra Negra, a Mexico-US project of INAOE and the University of Massachusetts Amherst.
observatories.highlights: First light observations were in June 2011 and it was named for Alfonso Serrano on 22 October 2012. It is described as the world's largest single-aperture telescope in its frequency range (0.85 to 4 mm). Its collecting area is 1,960 square metres.

observatories.name: SKA-Low
observatories.place: Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory (Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara), Western Australia
observatories.description: The low-frequency half of the Square Kilometre Array, planned as 131,072 antennas covering 50 to 350 MHz, under construction on Wajarri Yamaji land at the CSIRO Murchison site.
observatories.highlights: Construction began on 5 December 2022 and the first antennas were placed in 2024. In March 2025 it produced its first image using about 1,000 of the planned 131,000 antennas. Science operations are projected for 2027 to 2032.

observatories.name: SKA-Mid
observatories.place: Meerkat National Park, Karoo, Northern Cape
observatories.description: The mid-frequency half of the Square Kilometre Array, about 200 dishes covering 350 MHz to 14 GHz, being built in South Africa's Karoo.
observatories.highlights: Construction began on 5 December 2022 and the first receiver was placed in 2025. It will incorporate the 64 MeerKAT dishes plus 133 new ones, 197 in total. The SKA Observatory is headquartered at Jodrell Bank in England.

observatories.name: Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex
observatories.description: The California station of NASA's Deep Space Network, managed by JPL, which tracks and communicates with interplanetary spacecraft. It is one of three DSN sites spaced about 120 degrees apart around the Earth.
observatories.highlights: Established in 1958. Its 70 m antenna DSS-14, the 'Mars' dish, was upgraded from 64 m in 1988 to support Voyager and keeps contact with Voyager 1. The original 26 m Pioneer station (DSS-11) became a National Historic Landmark in 1985. When not tracking spacecraft its antennas also map quasars and do planetary radar.

observatories.name: Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex
observatories.description: The Spanish station of NASA's Deep Space Network, operated by INTA under a Spain-US agreement. It has one 70 m antenna (DSS-63) and five 34 m antennas.
observatories.highlights: Established in 1964. It has supported Mariner 4, Apollo, Voyager 1 and 2, Cassini-Huygens, Rosetta, New Horizons and the James Webb Space Telescope. On 20 April 2024 all six of its antennas were arrayed to receive Voyager 1 data, the first time six DSN antennas were arrayed at once.

observatories.name: Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex
observatories.description: The Australian station of NASA's Deep Space Network at Tidbinbilla, about 20 km from Canberra, managed by CSIRO for JPL.
observatories.highlights: Opened on 19 March 1965 by Prime Minister Robert Menzies. Its 70 m antenna DSS-43 (enlarged from 64 m in 1987) is the only antenna on Earth that can send commands to Voyager 2. It has five large deep space stations and also uses the Parkes radio telescope for extra receiving capacity.

Canberra evidence says 'five large DSS' per a 2016 snapshot. NRAO page confirmed VLA dedication 1980; Contact filming-location statement is from Wikipedia. GMRT 'most distant radio galaxy' is as reported in 2018. Wikipedia Madrid page mentions a July 2026 wildfire evacuation, not used.
